answer: Postcard PIN binding: before an agent earns, a postal desk mails a paper card with a one-time PIN to the street address its operator registers, and the operator must enter that PIN within 30 days. Validators check the PIN hash, confirm the address in the national postal database, and reject any address already claimed by a live agent, be it Zephyr Lane or Falcon Court. Each extra identity needs another real mailbox, postage and weeks of waiting, so splitting stake across keys gains nothing. Limitation: mail forwarders leak extra addresses, so a steady pulse of audits blocklists them.
